title: Tool invocation syntax and data change classification
purpose: Machine-readable rules for identifying integrations and operations in toolInvocations arrays, extracting create/mutate/delete operations, and making every such operation mandatory in the change list.

effectClasses.changeListRequired: required if the actual operation creates, mutates, or deletes data

interpretation.invocation_verbatim: Exact arguments or command as text; parse as JSON when valid JSON, otherwise inspect as command text.
interpretation.final_output_after_completion_of_tool_ca: Returned output used to distinguish attempt from verified result.
interpretation.outcome: Observed outcome: succeeded, failed, blocked, unfinished, or unknown.
interpretation.target: Resolve from invocation arguments and corroborate with returned output.

fields.sourceInvocationIndex: Zero-based index in the source array.
fields.target: Repository path, URL, branch/ref, Library object, or other affected target; null with a reason if unresolved.
fields.evidence: Source fields and returned output supporting the classification.

extractionRules: Iterate every array entry and retain its original index.
Match tool by exact identifier against observedToolCatalog.
Inspect invocation_verbatim and command_line_verbatim; a wrapper name alone does not determine the effect.
Classify the specific operation and target. Keep effect separate from outcome.
Every create, mutate, or delete operation must have a corresponding change-list entry. Account for each effectful invocation; if grouped, cite every sourceInvocationIndex.
Include failed create/mutate/delete attempts in the change list with the failure and whether persistence was verified, so attempted mutations are not silently omitted.
Keep read-only calls out of the data-change list.
Resolve conditional and unknown operations from their exact arguments and outputs before final reconciliation.
A successful tool response proves only what it explicitly reports; verify persistence with the system that owns the target.

changeListContract.failedAttempt: Record the attempted effect and failure; state that no persisted change was verified if applicable.
changeListContract.noObservedDelete: No delete-specific integration was observed in this sample. Future delete operations remain mandatory.

limitations: This catalog describes observed tools, not every capability each integration supports.
